He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa Hawkeyes]], where he was the consensus pick for [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|national college player of the year]] for the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]]. As a junior he was named a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Player of the Year]]. Garza played for [[Maret School]] in his hometown of [[Washington, D.C.]], where he was a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]]. ==Early life and high school career== Garza grew up in the Virginia suburbs of [[Washington, D.C.]] He learned to play [[basketball]] from his father, Frank, who played for [[Idaho Vandals men's basketball|Idaho]]. Garza watched [[video tape]]s that his father collected of former [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) post players like [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] and attempted to recreate their moves.{{cite web |last1=Emmert |first1=Mark |title=Iowa's Luka Garza studies the masters in attempt to become elite scorer |url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/college/iowa/2019/02/06/iowa-hawkeyes-basketball-indiana-hoosiers-luka-garza-old-school-mentality-years-studying-nba-greats/2783484002/ |website=Hawk Central |access-date=December 13, 2019 |date=February 6, 2019}} He stood {{height|ft=6|in=7}} as a freshman attending [[Maret School]] in Washington, D.C., but was not able to [[slam dunk|dunk]] a basketball until he was a sophomore. In high school, Garza was coached by [[Chuck Driesell]], son of [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Basketball Hall of Fame]] coach [[Lefty Driesell]].{{cite web |last1=Feinstein |first1=John |title=Iowa's Luka Garza is a rising star, and Lefty Driesell has been saying it for years |url=https://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/iowas-luka-garza-is-a-rising-star-and-lefty-driesell-has-been-saying-it-for-years-20190322 |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |access-date=December 13, 2019 |date=March 22, 2019}} In his senior season, he averaged 24.6 points, 11.7 rebounds and 2.5 blocks per game. Garza led Maret to the [[District of Columbia State Athletic Association]] (DCSAA) title game and earned D.C. [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] honors.{{cite web |last1=Whooley |first1=Connor |title=Iowa hoops commit Luke Garza wins Washington, D.C., Gatorade Player of the Year |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/college/iowa-hoops-commit-luke-garza-wins-washington-gatorade-player-the-year/Ien6Fkqt2gbaiVl59OPx3K/ |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |access-date=December 13, 2019 |date=March 20, 2017}} He left as his school's all-time leading scorer, with 1,993 points.{{cite web |last1=Mullan |first1=Dillon |title=Maret big man Luka Garza wins D.C. Gatorade Player of the Year |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/recruiting-insider/wp/2017/03/21/maret-big-man-luka-garza-wins-d-c-gatorade-player-of-the-year/ |website=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=December 13, 2019 |date=March 21, 2017}} ===Recruiting=== He was a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and chose to play college basketball for [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] over offers from [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|Georgia]] and [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]], among others.{{cite web |last1=Goodwin |first1=Cody |title=Four-star big man Luka Garza commits to Iowa hoops |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/high-school/recruiting/2016/09/10/four-star-big-man-luke-garza-commits-iowa-hoops/90135362/ |website=[[The Des Moines Register]] |access-date=December 13, 2019 |date=September 10, 2016}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Luka Garza | position = [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = [[Washington, D.C.]] | highschool = [[Maret School]] (DC) | feet = 6 | inches = 11 | weight = 265 | 40 = | commitdate = September 10, 2016 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 83 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2017 | rivals ref title = Iowa 2017 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2017 Iowa Hawkeyes Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = | rivals school = iowa | 247 school = | espn schoolid = 2294 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 111 | 247 overall = 105 | espn overall = 100 | accessdate = May 28, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Luka Garza.jpg|thumb|upright|Garza (right) in December 2019]] In his college debut versus [[Chicago State Cougars men's basketball|Chicago State]], Garza had 16 points. He had his first double-double of 11 points and 13 rebounds the following game in a win over [[Alabama State Hornets men's basketball|Alabama State]] and was named [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] freshman of the week.{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111317aab.html|title=Iowa and Minnesota Earn First Weekly Men’s Basketball Honors: Minnesota’s Jordan Murphy earns Player of the Week honors; Hawkeyes’ Luka Garza named Freshmen of the Week|access-date=November 13, 2017|date=November 13, 2017|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=BigTen.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171114040206/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111317aab.html|archive-date=November 14, 2017|url-status=dead}} As a freshman, Garza averaged 12.1 points and 6.4 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=Sophomore Luka Garza on a tear for surging Hawkeyes |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2019/02/05/sophomore-luka-garza-on-a-tear-for-surging-hawkeyes/39012409/ |access-date=December 15, 2019 |work=[[USA Today]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 5, 2019}} Shortly before his sophomore season, Garza underwent surgery to remove a {{convert|9|lb|kg|spell=in|adj=on}} [[cyst]] attached to his [[spleen]].{{cite web |title=Iowa C Luka Garza shooting for opener after cyst removed |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/10/08/iowa-c-luka-garza-shooting-for-opener-after-cyst-removed/38094647/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=October 8, 2018}}{{cite news |last1=Eickholt |first1=David |title=Luka Garza is "as tough of a player as you're going to find" |url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa/Article/Iowa-Hawkeyes-Basketball-Luka-Garza-Dan-Dakich-ESPN-Fran-McCaffery-All-American-Big-Ten-Conference--140516875/ |access-date=December 15, 2019 |work=247 Sports |date=December 14, 2019}} He also dealt with a sprained ankle in January 2019. In the NCAA Tournament, Garza had 20 points and seven rebounds to help Iowa upset [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]]. He averaged 13.1 points and 4.5 rebounds per game as a sophomore.{{cite news |last1=Meredith |first1=Luke |title=Luka Garza's Monster Start Propels Surging Hawkeyes |url=https://collegebasketball.ap.org/article/luka-garzas-monster-start-propels-surging-hawkeyes |access-date=December 15, 2019 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 5, 2019}} Garza was named All-Big Ten honorable mention by the media.{{Cite web |url=http://bigten.org/news/2019/3/11/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx?path=mbball |title=Big Ten Unveils Men's Basketball Postseason Honors on BTN |website=BigTen.org |date=March 11, 2019 |access-date=December 15, 2019 |df=mdy-all}} Garza scored 44 points, third-most in Iowa history, in a 103–91 loss to [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] on December 6.{{cite news |last1=Kahn |first1=Andrew |title=Luka Garza dropped 44 points on Michigan but it didn’t matter |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2019/12/luka-garza-dropped-44-points-on-michigan-but-it-didnt-matter.html |access-date=December 15, 2019 |work=MLive |date=December 7, 2019}} He followed this up with 21 points and 10 rebounds in a 72–52 win over [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] and was named Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week.{{cite news |last1=Eickholt |first1=David |title=Luka Garza named Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week |url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa/Article/Iowa-Hawkeyes-Basketball-Luka-Garza-Oscar-Robertson-Big-Ten-Conference-Michigan-Wolverines-140245942/ |access-date=December 15, 2019 |work=247 Sports |date=December 10, 2019}} In an 84–68 win against [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] on December 12, Garza had a tooth jarred loose after taking an elbow from teammate [[Joe Wieskamp]]. Garza returned to the game and finished with 21 points and 11 rebounds.{{cite news |last1=Creglow |first1=Zach |last2=Emmert |first2=Mark |title=Iowa star Luka Garza has tooth jarred loose, returns to [[Spanish American]] origin, and his mother is from Bosnia and Herzegovina, of [[Bosniaks|Bosniak]] origin. Both of Garza's parents have [[basketball]] experience: his father, Frank, played collegiately at [[Idaho Vandals men's basketball|Idaho]], and his mother, Šejla ([[née]] Muftić), played professionally in Europe. His grandfather on his father's side, James Halm, played college basketball for [[Hawaii Rainbow Warriors men's basketball|Hawaii]].
